verdict.rationale: RunAnywhere shows vendor-specific acceleration, but only for Apple and Qualcomm silicon. It runs on the Qualcomm Hexagon NPU on Snapdragon devices, its proprietary MetalRT engine uses Metal 3.1 GPU features on Apple M3 and later (M1/M2 fall back to llama.cpp), and an agentic pipeline validates kernels against the target silicon. Nothing in the evidence mentions NVIDIA or AMD GPU support, which is the core of the story. missing for 10: NVIDIA GPU kernels (e.g. CUDA), AMD GPU kernels (e.g. ROCm), documentation of which desktop GPU vendors are supported, independent benchmarks on NVIDIA/AMD hardware.
